nodes.name: Microwave plasma P-doping of Os/WC
nodes.procedure: P-doping was applied to Os nanocluster-supported WC substrates using microwave plasma technology (60 s), causing lattice expansion (XRD peak negative shift) and resulting in Os/P-WC with 0.62 wt% Os content. The process is illustrated in Fig. 1a (detailed procedures in Supplementary Information).

unit_operations.name: Microwave Plasma Doping
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: P-doping on Os nanocluster-supported WC substrates has been successfully achieved using microwave plasma technology

nodes.source_text: P-doping on Os nanocluster-supported WC substrates has been successfully achieved using microwave plasma technology, with its preparation process illustrated in Fig. 1a (see Supplementary information for detailed experimental procedures). X-ray diffraction (XRD) results indicate... diffraction peaks exhibit a negative shift relative to those of Os/WC.

nodes.source_text: Os/P-WC exhibits the lowest overpotential of 20 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm-2 (Fig. S9)... lowest overpotential of only 247 mV at 500 mA cm-2 (Fig. 3b)... exhibits the smallest Tafel slopes (Fig. 3c)... higher C_dl value (Fig. 3d)... highest TOF of 6.9 H2 s-1 and 12.9 H2 s-1 at overpotentials of 50 and 100 mV (Fig. 3f)... no significant activity degradation after 100 h... at current densities of 10 and 500 mA cm-2 (Fig. 3i)

Os/P-WC exhibits the lowest overpotentials... measuring 11 and 294 mV, respectively... highest MA of 0.29 A mg_Os^-1 and 0.92 A mg_Os^-1 at overpotentials of 10 and 50 mV... smallest Tafel slope of Os/P-WC (45.5 mV dec^-1)... higher C_dl values... highest TOF values of 9.0 H2 s^-1 and 17.5 H2 s^-1... after 100 h of continuous operation... activity remains largely intact

The HER performance of Os/P-WC was further evaluated in acidic media and the overpotential at 10 and 500 mA cm-2 were only 51 and 197 mV, respectively... outstanding MA of 0.011 A mg_Os^-1 and 0.13 A mg_Os^-1 at overpotentials of 10 and 40 mV... TOFs of 2.9 H2 s^-1 and 22.1 H2 s^-1 at 50 and 100 mV overpotentials... negligible activity loss after 70 h of continuous operation at 10 mA cm-2

nodes.characterization_summary: Os/P-WC shows hexagonal WC (PDF#51-0939) with diffraction peaks negatively shifted relative to Os/WC due to P-doping induced lattice expansion; no Os peaks observed due to small particle size or low content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) results indicate that the synthesized catalysts primarily consist of hexagonal WC (PDF#51-0939) ... no diffraction peaks corresponding to Os are observed in Os/P-WC

nodes.characterization_summary: Os content in Os/P-WC is 0.62 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) was constructed to analyze the content of Os, the result reveals that the Os content in Os/P-WC is only 0.62 wt%

nodes.characterization_summary: Os/P-WC shows rougher particle surface compared with WC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscope (SEM) images reveal the rougher particle surface of Os/P-WC compared with WC

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms increased surface roughness of Os/P-WC resulting in higher density of active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) further confirms the increased surface roughness of Os/P-WC

properties.description: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image showing nanostructured material with dark contrast regions and porous morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.23 nm for Os/P-WC and 0.21 nm for WC, both corresponding to (100) crystal plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) characterization reveals that the lattice spacing of Os/P-WC is 0.23 nm, while that of WC is 0.21 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of W, C, Os, and P in Os/P-WC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images confirm the uniform distribution of W, C, Os and P within Os/P-WC

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows W-C stretching vibrations at 700 and 800 cm⁻¹; Os/P-WC peak positions show no shift relative to WC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the stretching vibrations at 700 and 800 cm⁻¹ correspond to the W–C bond ... The peak position of Os/P-WC presents no shift relative to those of WC

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms successful Os loading and P doping on WC. C 1s peaks at 288.8 eV (C=O), 286.3 eV (C-O), 284.8 eV (C-C), 282.6 eV (C-W). Os 4f binding energies show negative shift and W 4f positive shift in Os/P-WC vs Os/WC, indicating P-doping enhanced EMSI creating electron-enriched Os sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The survey spectra demonstrate the successful loading of Os and the doping of P onto WC ... In the Os/P-WC system, the W 4f binding energy exhibits a further positive shift relative to Os/WC, while the Os 4f binding energy undergoes a more negative shift

nodes.characterization_summary: Work function values: Os/P-WC 4.6 eV, Os/WC 4.9 eV, WC 5.7 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the work function (WF) values of Os/P-WC, Os/WC, and WC were calculated to be 4.6, 4.9, and 5.7 eV, respectively via ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS)

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows broad peak 3000-3700 cm⁻¹ for interfacial water; peaks at 3250, 3450 cm⁻¹ for 4-HB and 3-HB water decrease with overpotential; K⁺·H₂O peak at 3615 cm⁻¹ indicates water decomposition; steeper Stark slope for K⁺·H₂O (49.9 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹) confirms stronger water interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ Raman tests were conducted in 1 M KOH ... the Stark tuning rate of the O–H stretching vibration mode (ν-OH) on the Os/P-WC surface following the order: K⁺·H₂O (49.9 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹) > 3-HB-H₂O (33.1 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹) > 4-HB-H₂O (24.7 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹)
